description: Read the company's account health report: what to fix in its email setup. Returns eligibility (checks need more than 1,000 active subscribers and an email sent in the last 14 days; hasMinimumSubscribers and sentRecently say which is missing), settings (enabled, autonomy), nextRunAt, the latest run (status, AI summary, stats snapshot of this period vs the one before) and runInProgress, plus open and snoozed insights, most severe first. Each insight has a detector (unhandled_event, stalled_sequence, campaign_gap, stale_campaign_drafts, underperforming_sequence_email, deliverability_spike, sending_domain_failing, missing_sequence: a standard lifecycle sequence such as welcome or re-engagement the workspace does not run yet, with the suggested playbook, name, goal, trigger and steps in evidence; over_emailing: people who got 4+ marketing emails within 24 hours in the last 7 days, with overloadedSubscribers, recipients, peakPerDay, frequencyCap and the campaigns, sequences and marketing Send API email (type api, which the cap does not limit) behind it as sources in evidence, where a sequence with enrollsEveryTime and peakEnrollmentsPerPerson 3 or more re-enrolls the same people and is fixed first with update_sequence enrollmentMode one_time; neglected_subscribers: active subscribers who got no marketing email in 90 days, with neglectedSubscribers, eligibleSubscribers and estimated in evidence; unengaged_signups: contacts who joined in the last 60 days with the same consumer mailbox provider (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook; business domains are never reported) and first list, got 2+ emails each and almost never opened or clicked while other new signups do, usually a bot filling a signup form or a bought list, with provider, providerLabel, listId, listName, emailed, sends, engaged, baselineEmailed and baselineEngaged in evidence), severity, title, detail, recommendation fixAutomationId when the agent drafted an inactive sequence to fix it, and actions: what to do about it, primary first. Each action has kind (create_sequence, open_sequence, activate_sequence, pause_sequence, create_campaign, review_campaign_drafts, open_campaign, verify_sending_domain, open_domain_settings, review_deliverability, open_frequency_cap_settings, apply_frequency_cap, review_subscribers), label, targetId, a dashboard path for screens, a confirm prompt for changes to live sending, and the api call that performs it: create_sequence -> create_account_health_fix, activate_sequence -> enable_sequence, pause_sequence -> disable_sequence, verify_sending_domain -> verify_sending_domain, open_frequency_cap_settings -> set_frequency_cap (for example maxEmails 1, windowHours 16) when evidence.frequencyCap is null, otherwise get_frequency_cap and only tighten it (the cap only holds back sequences, so when the sources are only campaigns or api it does not help; suggest spacing those out instead), apply_frequency_cap -> update_sequence with frequencyCapEnabled true on targetId (only on sequences that can wait, such as tips and nudges, not welcome or onboarding); the others open dashboard screens. Each insight also has feedback: the API key owner's own answer from submit_account_health_feedback ({rating, comment, updatedAt}), or null. Confirm with the user before set_frequency_cap or apply_frequency_cap. Confirm with the user before activate_sequence or pause_sequence. Requires analytics:read.
